findings.claim: JSDoc for excludeOperatorFamily is misleading: it says undefined means auto-detect via detectSupabase, but the auto-fallback is driven by the permissions.isSuperuser check inside installCommand.
Restrict permissions on the written .env.production.local file. writeFileSync writes production credentials (CS_CLIENT_KEY) with the default umask (typically 0o644, world-readable).
flush() is not idempotent despite the JSDoc claim; render() iterates over the full entries array each time, so calling flush() twice writes duplicate entries.
force: true silently overwrites user customizations in .claude/skills/<name>/; the confirm prompt doesn't mention that existing files will be clobbered.

Early return on the first existing candidate dir may skip the real migrations directory; rewriteEncryptedMigrations returns on the first DRIZZLE_OUT_DIRS entry that exists regardless of whether it contains the emitted migrations.
Duplicate matches when a single line triggers multiple kinds (e.g. .from(users) and .update(users) on one line), producing two report entries for the same source position.

findings.claim: Auto-fallback triggers on !isSuperuser regardless of whether permissions are already sufficient, so non-superuser roles with explicit grants are silently downgraded to the no-operator-family variant.
err.message duplicates noise now that stderr streams to the terminal; logging it mostly restates the generic 'Command failed' text.
process.exit(1) is used instead of the p.cancel + return pattern used by other cancellation paths, skipping future cleanup and making the function harder to test.
Redundant defaultValue/initialValue pairing in the clientPath prompt.
Generated config uses non-null assertion on DATABASE_URL; if unset, downstream code receives undefined and fails with a less helpful error than an explicit throw.
Use path.join instead of manual string concatenation; hard-coded forward slashes won't handle Windows paths cleanly.
.pooler.supabase.com is already covered by .supabase.com; the third branch is dead.
"Next.js precedence" isn't exactly Next.js: .env.development is loaded unconditionally regardless of NODE_ENV.

Back-compat detection is correct, but the parallel implementation in packages/drizzle only emits/detects the bare eql_v2_encrypted form; if it is updated to emit the schema-qualified form its detection would silently miss encrypted columns.
detectDrizzle(process.cwd()) hard-codes the working directory instead of threading cwd through as an option.
